description: Event-name canonicalization (Issue #36 / D-34). Verifies framework events are emitted with the canonical apcore.<subsystem>.<event> form, that legacy names are dual-emitted with deprecated:true during the v0.21.x cycle, that glob subscriptions match canonical names, and that health-threshold events use the apcore.health.* subsystem.

test_cases.description: An apcore.registry.* glob subscription MUST receive both module_registered and module_unregistered canonical events.
An apcore.health.* glob subscription MUST receive recovered + threshold-exceeded events under the canonical apcore.health.* namespace.

Threshold-crossing events MUST be emitted under apcore.health.* (not apcore.error.* / apcore.latency.*). The p99 value is asserted as `data_at_least`, not an exact match: every SDK estimates p99 from histogram BUCKET BOUNDS, and the bucket layout is not fixed by the spec — apcore-rust's DEFAULT_BUCKETS has no 6.0s boundary and reports 10000.0 for a 6s sample. The canonical event NAME is still asserted exactly, which is what this case is for. Also carries the inverse assertion for the HEALTH legacy aliases removed at v0.22.0 (apcore#78): this is the only trigger that could emit them, so it is the only place the assertion is not vacuous.
apcore.registry.* MUST NOT match apcore.health.* events.

Dual-emission ended at v0.22.0 (apcore#78): a conformant SDK MUST emit the canonical name ONLY. This case replaces `legacy_dual_emit` and `legacy_health_dual_emit`, which required the v0.21.x dual emit and which no v0.22+ SDK could satisfy without violating the current MUST in features/event-system.md. Keeping the inverse assertion means the removal stays pinned instead of merely deleted. Scope note: this case's trigger is `registry.register`, so it can only pin the REGISTRY legacy names. An earlier revision also listed `apcore.error.threshold_exceeded` and `apcore.latency.threshold_exceeded` here, which no implementation could emit on a registration path — half the assertion was vacuous. Those two moved to `health_threshold_canonical`, whose trigger can actually produce them.

driver_contract.forbidden_names_need_a_reachable_trigger: A `forbidden_event_types` entry is only an assertion if the case's trigger could plausibly emit it. Listing a health-threshold name under a `registry.register` trigger asserts nothing — no implementation emits it on that path — while making the case look twice as thorough. Each forbidden name is placed on the case whose trigger can actually produce it.
